rows.check: NetworkInterface recognizes the complete locked admin, packet, state, property, counter, and observer vocabulary; the historical open/stop surface rejects.
Carrier and portable operational state are present; speed, duplex, autonegotiation, and supported-mode negotiation remain provider-specific L2 data.
No standalone flow-control primitive is introduced; provider-specific pause policy remains outside the locked interface table.
Linux transmit rejection maps to NETDEV_TX_BUSY with caller ownership retained; queue stop/wake mechanics remain native and absent from L1.
The locked read_counters operation exposes portable traffic counters; named ethtool sets and device accumulation mechanics remain L2.
MTU is a capability-gated property; ring geometry, reallocation, and restart choreography are absent from NIM IR.
PHY/MII and media control remain ordinary device/provider logic and are not added to NetworkInterface.
ReceiveFilterMode is a property value while address lists, VLAN tables, and native filter programming remain L2.
Offload and feature negotiation are deliberately excluded from the frozen surface and generated portable table.
OpaquePacketBuffer carries only backend identity; Linux skb and Zephyr net_pkt layout, fragments, checksum, VLAN, GSO, and mutation stay native.
Synchronous acceptance/refusal is independent from terminal completion; generated output states no per-packet completion is fabricated.
Wake-on-LAN remains power/provider policy and is absent from NetworkInterface.
EEPROM access remains device register/management behavior, not network administration vocabulary.
Register dumps, self-test, and physical-ID LED control remain device diagnostics outside the locked element.
Interrupt coalescing metadata and operations remain backend/provider-owned and absent from L1.
Linux descriptor/index/DMA/IRQ/deferred-work composition and Zephyr native packet helpers are tested without adding NAPI or poll budgets to L1.
Management firmware and ASF lifecycle behavior are not forced into NetworkInterface.
PCI error recovery remains lifecycle/error-recovery ownership; NIM supplies no AER callbacks.
Portable model/source negative checks forbid descriptors, indices, DMA mappings, IRQ bindings, work queues, and polling budgets in NIM.
Name, index, MTU, and link address use native Linux/Zephyr identity/property sources; no default-MAC binding is invented.
